Trump's Russia diesel deal faces criticism amid Ukraine conflict

President Donald Trump announced an "energy ceasefire" between Russia and Ukraine, stating that Russian President Vladimir Putin desires a deal more than Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. This announcement followed reports of a "diesel deal" between Trump and Putin for importing Russian diesel, which has drawn criticism from a "frustrated Congress" and "GOP heartburn" before a vote. Ukraine has accused Russia of violating an energy ceasefire, and some reports indicate energy prices have risen as the ceasefire has not moved Russia or Ukraine. Ukrainians are reportedly feeling "extremely betrayed" by the deal. Meanwhile, Zelenskyy has welcomed the US-announced energy ceasefire and called for "more pressure" on Russia, while also warning of a global grain crisis and stating there are "no signs Russia wants to end the war."
